scene-u01-pnew2-4.name: text#4
scene-u01-pnew2-4.text: Rigid direct subtraction breaks with a small shift: the distance is distorted and the wrong template wins

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: Point-wise subtraction measures misalignment, not similarity; so each kind of variation needs its own distance $D$.

scene-u01-pnew2-19.name: text#19
scene-u01-pnew2-19.text: Orange area: differences squared and summed (horizontal: position $x$)

scene-u01-pnew2-22.name: text#22
scene-u01-pnew2-22.text: A shift of only $0.02$ ($2\%$ of the range) raises the distance from $0$ to $1.08$.

scene-u01-pnew2-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew2-25.text: Distance rises with shift, then saturates

scene-u01-pnew2-47.name: text#47
scene-u01-pnew2-47.text: Shift $\delta$ (once pulses stop overlapping, distance stops growing)

scene-u01-pnew2-50.name: text#50
scene-u01-pnew2-50.text: The nearest template can be wrong

scene-u01-pnew2-59.name: text#59
scene-u01-pnew2-59.text: Test $t$ is really $r$ shifted by $0.12$, yet picking the smallest distance assigns it to $q$.
